about: Product facts the history checkers read. A row that states a number carries its cite (a page or source line at read_at). If the pages change a number, this file changes with them, never the checker.

reader.about: The product's code for reading an observation and placing an operation from it: checkers/product_block.py, loaded by file (the checkers run under python -I).

bounds_note: C6 latency bounds, rows of {verb, seconds, cite}. The operator pages state no bound on the duration of any operation, so there is no row and every verb is listed as not judged. Only a bound a page states goes here, never an invented number.

recovery.what: a holder that crashed is re-granted at most this long after it stopped
the holder's start wait ends this long after the re-grant or after its start, whichever is later

recovery_note: A holder is healthy again by max(kill completion + regrant, restart completion) + start_wait. The pages state no restart bound for the master: its restart is not judged.

master_outage.what: volumes already serving keep serving through a master restart this short: each holder renews every 10 s or less and may serve until 20 s after its last renewal, so a master that answers again within 10 s interrupts nothing. A longer outage is not judged by MO (it is fail-closed, with its own recovery bound).

holder_unit.what: the product's shipped unit for blockvolume. The runner plays it for every holder it launched and reads its policy (Restart, RestartPreventExitStatus, RestartSec, TimeoutStopSec) from this file at the product commit the run built, never from a copy here; if the file cannot be read or parsed, it refuses to emulate. A holder the runner killed itself is left to the fault schedule's restart.

fault_targets.name: blockmaster
fault_targets.what: the block master daemon; a kill of it reaches no holder, so no volume's data path

fault_targets.name: blockvolume:<i>
fault_targets.what: the block volume daemon holding volume i (from 0); a process whose name starts with the prefix is a holder

block_bytes.what: the block size in bytes on first create (the daemon's --durable-blocksize default; the runner also passes 4096); the checkers' ZERO is the sha256 of one block of zeros

placement.cite: docs/operator-guide.md:222-223 (the volume's data is committed either way; the snapshot name exists only after a request for it succeeds)
placement.what: an unknown snapshot is placed by HEAD's snapshot names (the observation's snapshots field) after it, against the observation before it: its name already there before it cannot place it; another name lost is a third state; its name there after it: it took effect; absent: it did not. The checker's C6 (product_block.py) and the driver's rerun read this row; when neither observation records the names, the checker places by the root/ objects (its own code) and the driver re-issues nothing

placement_note: The placement table, one row per verb placed by a list of names; a closed vocabulary: by is list_member (the request's name in the observation's list field), the four cases are present_before, others_lost, present and absent, and each maps to one of took_effect, did_not, third, not_placed.

release_on_delete.cite: core/frontend/chunkstore/layout/delete.go:176-183 (DeleteVolume: once the target's HEAD is deleting, the target is released from each source it depends on), :146-151 (RunReleaseDependent: one conditional update of the source's HEAD), :92-119 (ReleaseDependent changes only the dependents of the source's snapshots; a source with no such dependent is a replay and writes nothing), core/frontend/chunkstore/layout/head.go:519-539 (runTransition: the update advances the source's HEAD generation by one, :537); docs/design/invariants.md:1097 (INV-SNAPK-RELEASE-001); the same lines at the rc.3 pin, the invariant at :1098
release_on_delete.why: a delete (ok or unknown) of a volume the history shows restored (ok) from a source releases it from the source's dependents: the source's HEAD generation moves LATER, by at most per_release x the number of such deletes invoked and completed between the two observations of the source (an ok delete counts 1, an unknown one 0 or 1: the bound is the ok count + the unknown count; a larger rise is a change), and nothing else: its epoch, holder and state, its snapshot names (the dependents are recorded in head_diag.snapshots, not compared), its files and its workspace answer stay equal. A refused delete allows nothing. Not a reset of the source's baseline: any other difference is still a change.

states.cite: core/authority/workspace_lease_view.go:221-275 (a live holder's renewal grants min(now + workspaceTTL, the durable horizon): the expiry moves at every renewal)
core/authority/workspace_lease_view.go:253-257 (revoking: tell the host to drain; never extend)

cmd/sw-block/workspace_show.go:54-58 (the three states: expired when no validity is left, revoking, else granted), core/authority/workspace_lease_view.go:259-261 (only a re-grant follows, and it shows granted again)

across_master_restart.cite: core/authority/authority.go:257 (workspaceTTL = 30 * time.Second), :316-322 (at the master's start every workspace lease's deadline is set to now + workspaceTTL: persisted wall time alone never shortens a live host's lease)
across_master_restart.no_restart_cite: core/authority/workspace_lease_view.go:306 (the extender starts when the durable horizon is less than now + 1.25 x workspaceTTL), :455 (it sets the horizon to its trigger + 1.5 x workspaceTTL, the trigger at or before the reading); core/authority/authority.go:257 (workspaceTTL = 30 s)
across_master_restart.skew_cite: core/authority/workspace_lease_view.go:154-157 (validity = max(0, min(expiry - skew/2 - now, workspaceTTL))), core/authority/workspace.go:116-124 (the skew is the configured bound, or a lease's persisted larger one), cmd/blockmaster/main.go:138 (--workspace-max-clock-skew, default 20 s; the runner does not set it, so no lease persists a larger one). The workspace show does not print the skew (cmd/sw-block/workspace_show.go:60)
across_master_restart.why: while a lease is in a state that does not renew (states, renews false) at both observations, its expiry IS compared, step or no step, and is MONOTONE: equal or later, never earlier. Across no master restart it is at most the later observation's reading end in wall time (from_wall_ns + mono_ns - from_mono_ns) + no_restart_ttl_factor x ttl_seconds + slack_seconds (the furthest the extender sets the horizon); in a history before from_wall_ns the reading end is mono_ns + the history's fit (expiry - skew/2 - validity - mono_ns, median over observations with 0 < validity < ttl), and with no fit that ceiling is not checked. A master restart re-arms each lease, so across a blockmaster restart record between the two it is at most the restart's wall time (its complete's started_wall_ns) + ttl_seconds + slack_seconds; every other kept fact equal, a lease-state step only as the time_derived table allows. In expired_state the printed expiry is at or before the reading's end in wall time + skew_seconds/2 (no validity is left: expiry - skew/2 <= now); checked only on an observation with from_wall_ns. In a renewing state (granted at either observation) the expiry is not compared (renewals move it). A history that records no restart's started_wall_ns at all (from before the field): across its master restart the expiry is not compared. NOTE: the v1.0.2 delete-ACK work (a recorded ACK ends the wait before the horizon) will change this row on purpose, and the row will then name that step. slack_seconds (2) covers the runner's wall time taken just after the restarted master holds its port, at or after the master's own now. Without a ceiling a lease that never expires would pass, and it blocks deletes and moves forever. A restart record without started_wall_ns (a history before it) in a history that records it elsewhere gets no allowance: the rule across no restart

time_derived.cite: cmd/sw-block/workspace_show.go:54-58 (expired exactly when the validity is <= 0, else revoking or granted), :60 (the expiry and the validity at query); docs/volume-lifecycle.md:35
time_derived.why: the lease state is derived from a fact (the lease's expiry) and the clock: it is the host validity at query time. A step listed here is time alone only when the fact is equal in both observations, the earlier observation's validity is not larger than the longest time that can lie between the two readings (the later observation's end, mono_ns, minus the earlier one's start, from_mono_ns), and every other kept fact is equal. Otherwise, and for any step not listed (time does not run backwards: expired to granted), it stays a change. An observation without from_mono_ns gives no bound, so no step is time alone.

observation.required_note: C5 requires these parts in both observations of a judged refusal: a pair lacking one leaves the refusal not judged (no PASS on what was not seen).

ignored.why: available from the filer listing in whole seconds (core/frontend/chunkstore/layout_store.go:344-346); not recorded: too coarse to order writes within an observation pair
not recorded by the observation: it keeps HEAD's generation, epoch, holder and state, the volume's identity, ownership and life state
recorded for diagnosis; not compared. Each claim writes a new one (core/frontend/chunkstore/layout/head.go:138-142)
recorded for diagnosis; not compared. It names the open transaction: a cleaning or snapshot session opens and closes with its own generation moves, so a generation rise names its writer
recorded for diagnosis; not compared. It moves with every committed write
recorded for diagnosis; not compared. It moves with every commit of a new image

ignored.field: head_diag.snapshots (HEAD's Snapshots: each snapshot's Root, Position, Meta and Dependents)
ignored.why: recorded for diagnosis; not compared. Only the snapshot names are compared (snapshots); the dependents move with a restore from the snapshot and with the delete of its target (release_on_delete); the roots appear in the file listing (files)
only the error code is compared: the exit status of a failed show says no more than its code

ignored.field: snapshots_error, dirs_error, listing_error, an unreadable head
ignored.why: not values: a part recorded with an error cannot be compared, and a refusal judged on it is left not judged
changes with every renewal; not a state a refusal can change. Not compared; kept only as the fact the lease state derives from (time_derived)
changes with every query; not a state a refusal can change. Not compared; kept only to bound a time_derived step
